game: GB @ DET Week 13 2025, kickoff 2025-11-27 13:00 ET, Ford Field dome, DET -2.5, total 48.5

script.base: Closing line only (open and moneyline not in the pack): Detroit is a short home favorite with implied totals DET 25.5 and GB 23.0 in a 48.5 dome game, so the book expects a close, high-play game and full starter snaps, not a blowout. Base flow is Detroit leaning on Jahmyr Gibbs as the engine (42 carries / 400 rush yards and 24 targets / 182 receiving yards in weeks 10-12) with Amon-Ra St. Brown as the pass hub (33 targets / 249 yards), while Green Bay, with Jayden Reed out, splits carries between Emanuel Wilson (40/149) and Josh Jacobs (28/114) and throws to Christian Watson, Romeo Doubs and Dontayvion Wicks. Both passing games have been better when blitzed, so Detroit's 32% blitz and Green Bay's 22% blitz do not point to a sack-driven slog.
script.flip1: Detroit gets up early on Gibbs explosives, then runs the clock. Gibbs and David Montgomery carries rise late, Green Bay abandons the run so Jacobs and Wilson rush yards stall, and Jordan Love funnels to Watson (16 targets / 287 air yards in the L3), Doubs and Wicks. Detroit receiver yardage can stall if the lead gets comfortable.
script.flip2: Detroit's offensive line cluster bites (Graham Glasgow already out; Taylor Decker, Penei Sewell, Tate Ratledge and Miles Frazier all questionable) and Green Bay's run defense (3.92 YPC, only 20 runs of 10+ in 11 games) holds. Gibbs' 9.5 YPC regresses, Detroit throws more to St. Brown and Jameson Williams, and Green Bay's thin receiver room still has to throw to keep up with a 23.0 implied total.

injury_fallout: Source: nflverse official injury report, pre-game. Final inactives about 90 minutes before kickoff are not in the pack, so every Questionable tag is unresolved. Detroit out: C Graham Glasgow (knee) weakens the interior in front of Gibbs and Montgomery; WR Kalif Raymond (ankle; 6 targets / 86 yards in weeks 10-12) and TE Brock Wright (neck; 12 targets / 37 yards) are out, so those looks tilt to St. Brown (already 33 targets), Jameson Williams, Sam LaPorta (pack L3 only 5 targets / 53 yards) and Gibbs (24 targets). S Kerby Joseph (knee) out and CB Terrion Arnold (concussion) questionable soften the back end for Green Bay deep targets, led by Watson's 287 air yards, but Watson has no listed prop. DE Joshua Paschal out and DE Marcus Davenport questionable. T Decker (shoulder), T Sewell (ankle), G Frazier (knee) and G Ratledge (knee) are all questionable; if the tackles sit, Gibbs' rushing efficiency is the first thing that dies. RB Sione Vaki (ankle) questionable is depth only. Green Bay out: WR Jayden Reed (foot) and WR Savion Williams (foot), so Doubs (15 targets / 81 yards), Wicks (14/79) and Watson (16/140) absorb a thin room; Matthew Golden is questionable (wrist). Tucker Kraft is not on the report and is also absent from the weeks 10-12 target list. Green Bay DE Lukas Van Ness (foot) and DT Karl Brooks (ankle) are out, which is the front Gibbs runs at; CB Keisean Nixon (neck), CB Nate Hobbs (knee) and LB Quay Walker (neck) are questionable, and Walker is the linebacker most relevant to Gibbs as a receiver.

Green Bay defense YPA left 5.52 (125), middle 7.15 (94), right 5.61 (145), so the middle is also Green Bay's soft spot, at a lower YPA.
matchup.pressure: Detroit blitz rate 32%; Green Bay EPA/dropback +0.38 vs blitz vs +0.21 vs none, so Love has been better when blitzed. Green Bay blitz rate 22%; Detroit EPA/dropback +0.27 vs blitz vs +0.10 clean. No pressure rate or time-to-throw in the pack. Pass-rush personnel: Green Bay DE Van Ness out and DT Karl Brooks out; Detroit DE Davenport questionable and DE Paschal out.
matchup.bleeds: Detroit run defense allows 4.11 YPC and 33 runs of 10+, plus 37 passes of 20+ yards (382). Green Bay is tighter on the ground (3.92 YPC, only 20 runs of 10+ in 11 games) and has allowed fewer explosives through the air (21 passes of 20+, 393 yards), so the explosives that do happen are long. Both defenses bleed the middle more than the outside.
matchup.overlap: Detroit's primary option is St. Brown (33 targets, 249 yards, 358 air yards in weeks 10-12), which maps onto Green Bay's middle bleed (7.15 YPA) and a banged-up secondary (Nixon and Hobbs questionable) plus a thinner pass rush (Van Ness and Brooks out). Gibbs (24 targets, 182 receiving yards) is the secondary overlap on that same middle/linebacker area, with Quay Walker questionable. Green Bay's deep overlap would be Watson (287 air yards on 16 targets) against Detroit S Joseph out and CB Arnold questionable, but Watson is not in the available props. No chart names the actual slot or nickel.

form: Using weeks 10-12 and the listed last-4 logs, not season averages. Gibbs last4 rush yards 25, 142, 39, 219; the last three sum to the pack's 400 rush yards on 42 carries (9.5 YPC) plus 182 receiving yards on 24 targets. Rush+rec last4 is 28, 172, 146, 264. Montgomery still has a slice (L3 26 carries / 116 rush yards and 5 targets / 29 receiving yards) but not the ceiling. St. Brown last4 receiving yards 97, 58, 42, 149, and 58+42+149 matches the L3 249. Jameson Williams last4 66, 119, 88, 0 and L3 17 targets / 207 yards / 164 air, including the zero. LaPorta's pack L3 line is only 5 targets / 53 yards / 19 air, which does not reconcile with last4 55, 15, 97, 53, so that conflict is flagged and he is not used. Green Bay: Wilson L3 40 carries / 149 yards with log 16, 2, 40, 107, so one game is most of the yards and a 2-yard game sits inside the same window. Jacobs' pack L3 is 28 carries / 114 yards, but last4 rush 33, 87, 74, 40 does not sum to 114, so that conflict is flagged and he is not used. Doubs L3 15 targets / 81 yards / 149 air (5.4 yards per target). Wicks L3 14/79/127. Kraft is missing from the L3 target list. Defense form is the 11-game lines above.

If Detroit leads late, the lead back's carries rise; Gibbs is both that back and a 24-target receiver, so he is in the script either way.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Gibbs has been the entire Detroit offense lately, about 194 scrimmage yards a game over weeks 10-12 (400 rush on 42 carries plus 182 receiving on 24 targets), and 99.5 still sits under that role even if Green Bay's run defense drags the rushing half down, because the catches travel with him whether Detroit leads or trails.
edge_players.must_be_true: Gibbs keeps the weeks 10-12 workload, about 14 carries and 8 targets, Detroit does not lose both tackle spots at inactives (Decker and Sewell are only questionable; Glasgow is already out), and a 2.5-point, 48.5 script keeps him on the field rather than handing the grind to Montgomery.
edge_players.kills_it: Sewell and Decker both sit, Green Bay's explosive-run suppression (20 runs of 10+ in 11 games, 3.92 YPC) bottles the ground game, and the passing work stays with St. Brown, reproducing the 25-rush / 3-receiving dud (28 scrimmage yards). A Montgomery takeover of the 26-carry L3 slice does the same thing.

data_check.notes: No projection sim and no Pinnacle, Circa or BetOnline no-vig in the pack, so the rung cannot be priced and the 3-point edge gate cannot be run. Hand check only: last4 rush+rec 28, 172, 146, 264 is 3 of 4 over 99.5 (0.75). Ratings in the 70-80% band are treated as suspicious. Green Bay's 11-game run defense (3.92 YPC, 20 runs of 10+) and Detroit's line cluster (Glasgow out; Decker, Sewell, Ratledge and Frazier questionable) disagree with repeating 9.5 YPC. They do not erase the receiving half (182 yards on 24 targets; GB middle 7.15 YPA). That is a disagreement with a strong usage read, so it is flagged for the human and not cut. model_p 0.58 is a hand discount from the 0.75 recent hit rate for the run-defense and offensive-line disagreement and for the 70% suspicion rule. It is not a sim probability and it is not a stake. No bet placed. Other leans were dropped rather than flagged: Jacobs rush under 70.5 fights a leaky Detroit run defense (4.11 YPC, 33 runs of 10+) and an irreconcilable last4 (33, 87, 74, 40 vs L3 114); Wilson rush over 21.5 is a 107-yard spike plus an in-window 2-yard game; St. Brown over 77.5 is only 83 vs 77.5 with two of the last four under (58, 42).

pre_mortem: It's Monday and this lost because Sewell and Decker were inactive, Glasgow's replacement could not create lanes, and Green Bay's 3.92 YPC defense with only 20 explosive runs in 11 games turned the 142- and 219-yard rushing games into a 25-yard grind. Montgomery's 26-carry share from the last three weeks took the red-zone and clock work, St. Brown kept the 11 targets a game, and Gibbs finished in the 28 scrimmage-yard neighborhood again. The 99.5 line was catching the two explosive games, not a repeatable floor, and there was no no-vig price to show the number was actually long.
slip_story: One-story slip: Detroit's engine in a competitive dome game (DET -2.5, total 48.5, implied 25.5). Gibbs rush+rec over is the lead-back volume leg that still works if Detroit leads (carries) or trails (targets). It is a single leg because no second available prop cleared the pre-mortem. Do not pair it with a game under, a Jacobs rush over, or a Montgomery rush over, which need a different touch distribution. St. Brown would have been the correlated pass piece, but 83 yards a game against 77.5 with two misses in the last four was too thin to add.
